description: Atomic facts on tilapia feeding, FCR, growth and temperature response, added 2026-11-26 for the Fish growth and feed checkpoint. Candidates until Ajit approves them (Batch 003). Reliability recorded per AGENTS.md 6A.

facts.statement: Tilapia feed conversion ratios of 1.4 to 1.8 are common; UVI's aquaponic Nile tilapia averaged 1.7.

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Three Tier 1 sources agree; no size breakdown.

facts.statement: Suggested tank-culture feeding rates for tilapia fall from 15-20 percent of body weight a day for fry under 0.5 g to 3-5 percent at 18-75 g and 1.5-3 percent from 75 g to market size.

review_metadata.confidence_reason: NCRAC 114 (NRC 1993, 28 C) and FAO AFFRIS Table 26b agree above 100 g.

approval.scope: truth FISH_0002 (D1: Tier 1-2, medium or high, corroborated)
approval.record: Approval Batch 003, approved as recommended (thread message 2026-11-26 05:54 Europe/Amsterdam)

facts.statement: Tilapia stop feeding below about 17 C (63 F).

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Two Tier 1 sources agree (17.2 and 17 C); a pond bioenergetic model uses 18.7 C.

approval.scope: truth FISH_0003 (D1: Tier 1-2, medium or high, corroborated)
approval.record: Approval Batch 003, approved as recommended (thread message 2026-11-26 05:54 Europe/Amsterdam)

facts.statement: Tilapia growth at the optimum temperature is typically about three times that at 22 C (72 F).

review_metadata.confidence_reason: A 2022 review gives about 30 percent of maximum at 20 to 22 C (secondary citation).

approval.scope: truth FISH_0004 (D1: Tier 1-2, medium or high, corroborated)
approval.record: Approval Batch 003, approved as recommended (thread message 2026-11-26 05:54 Europe/Amsterdam)

facts.statement: Optimum tilapia growth temperature is reported as 27 to 29 C (SRAC 282), 27 to 30 C (FAO TP 589) and 29 to 31 C (SRAC 283); acceptable growth 25 to 32 C.

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Sources overlap at 27 to 30 but differ at the top; kept as a context split.

corroboration.note: FAO CASIP 'preferred' 31 to 36 C is a behavioural preference, not a growth optimum.

facts.statement: In the UVI aquaponic system, all-male Nile tilapia grew from 79 g to 814 g in 24 weeks (4.4 g/day, FCR 1.7, 98 percent survival) at 77 fish per m3, harvesting 61.5 kg/m3 per tank, about 4.16 t a year from four 7.8 m3 tanks.

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Mean of 20 harvests; reproduced in SRAC 454 Table 1. The 5 t/yr design target is a different figure.

approval.scope: truth FISH_0006 (D1: Tier 1-2, medium or high, corroborated)
approval.record: Approval Batch 003, approved as recommended (thread message 2026-11-26 05:54 Europe/Amsterdam)

facts.statement: UVI fed its tilapia a complete floating pellet with 32 percent protein, ad libitum over 30 minutes, three times a day.

review_metadata.confidence_reason: SRAC 282 (32 to 40 percent finishing feed) and NCRAC 114 (28 to 32 percent above 40 g) agree.

approval.scope: truth FISH_0007 (D1: Tier 1-2, medium or high, corroborated)
approval.record: Approval Batch 003, approved as recommended (thread message 2026-11-26 05:54 Europe/Amsterdam)

facts.statement: No thermal growth coefficient or specific growth rate for Nile tilapia, and no FCR by fish size, was found in Tier 1 or 2 sources that could be opened.

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Candidate papers (Azaza et al. 2008) were behind bot checks.

facts.statement: Nile tilapia (three strains, 1.4 to 1.9 g start, 120 days) grew with an exponential rate constant of 0.0259 to 0.0285 per day at 22 C, against 0.0390 to 0.0419 at 28 C and 0.0374 to 0.0431 at 30 C.

context.species: Nile tilapia, Red, GIFT and Supreme strains

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Direct table values; consistent in direction with Likongwe 1996 and Workagegn 2014; Azaza 2008 numbers not obtained.
